docs.title: stratajanus
docs.text: stratajanus is a small educational search engine for exploring lexical information retrieval. Its implemented search path uses SciFact documents, a versioned tokenizer, an in-memory inverted index, and BM25 ranking.

docs.title: Current capabilities
docs.text:
• Download and validate the BEIR-format SciFact dataset.
  • Convert source records into normalized JSONL and TSV files with a manifest and stable document ID mapping.
  • Normalize and tokenize text consistently for indexing and queries.
  • Build an in-memory inverted index and rank matching documents with BM25.
  • Search processed SciFact from the command line.

The current index is rebuilt in memory and is not persisted. The project does not yet implement benchmark metric evaluation, learning-to-rank, dense or hybrid retrieval, RAG, or financial signal extraction. Those are possible future directions, not current search features.

docs.title: Retrieval pipeline
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[BEIR SciFact corpus] --> B[Prepare JSONL and ID mapping]
    B --> C[Tokenize title and text]
    C --> D[In-memory inverted index]
    Q[User query] --> E[Same tokenizer]
    E --> F[BM25 scores]
    D --> F
    F --> G[Ranked SearchResult values]

The prepared records retain their external SciFact doc_id. During index construction each document also receives a zero-based internal ID based on input order. Postings and document lengths use internal IDs; search results include both identifiers so the CLI can look up and display source documents. See the architecture and indexing pages for the data flow and structures.

docs.title: Install and run
docs.text:
Use Python 3.13 or newer, as specified by pyproject.toml. From the repository root:

python3.13 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -e .
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

The editable install installs the stratajanus package. requirements.txt provides the pinned development, SciFact, test, and MkDocs tools.

Run the test suite:

python -m pytest

Download and prepare SciFact, then build the in-memory index and search it:

python scripts/download_scifact.py
python scripts/prepare_scifact.py
python scripts/index_scifact.py
python scripts/search_scifact.py "evidence for a scientific claim" --top-k 10

The download and preparation commands create data under ignored data/ directories. index_scifact.py validates an in-memory build; it does not write an index artifact. search_scifact.py independently loads the processed documents and rebuilds the index for each invocation.

Preview the documentation locally with:

mkdocs serve

The API reference documents the package and dataset scripts.

def tokenize(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """
    Convert text into tokens using stratajanus' version-1 rules.

    Steps:
    1. Unicode-normalize using NFC.
    2. Lowercase.
    3. Extract non-overlapping matches of Python's Unicode-aware ``\\w+``.
       Letters, digits, and underscore are retained within matches; other
       characters separate them. Repeated tokens and source order are kept.

    Args:
        text: Unicode string to analyze.

    Returns:
        Tokens in their order of appearance. Punctuation-only or empty input
        returns an empty list.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If ``text`` is not a string.
    """
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        raise TypeError(
            f"tokenize() expected str, got {type(text).__name__}"
        )

    normalized = unicodedata.normalize(
        CONFIG.unicode_normalization,
        text,
    )

    if CONFIG.lowercase:
        normalized = normalized.lower()

    return TOKEN_REGEX.findall(normalized)

def save_tokenizer_config(path: Path) -> None:
    """Write active tokenizer settings as formatted UTF-8 JSON.

    Args:
        path: Destination file path.

    Returns:
        None. Parent directories are created as needed and an existing file is
        overwritten.
    """
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as file:
        json.dump(
            asdict(CONFIG),
            file,
            indent=2,
            ensure_ascii=False,
        )
        file.write("\n")

def verify_tokenizer_config(path: Path) -> None:
    """Check that a saved tokenizer configuration matches :data:`CONFIG`.

    Args:
        path: UTF-8 JSON configuration file to read.

    Returns:
        None when the decoded JSON equals the active configuration.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If the path does not exist.
        json.JSONDecodeError: If the file is not valid JSON.
        ValueError: If the saved settings differ from the active settings.
    """
    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as file:
        saved_config = json.load(file)

    current_config = asdict(CONFIG)

    if saved_config != current_config:
        raise ValueError(
            "Tokenizer configuration does not match the index.\n"
            f"Saved:   {saved_config}\n"
            f"Current: {current_config}"
        )

@dataclass
class InvertedIndex:
    """Hold postings and per-document statistics for an in-memory collection.

    Args:
        postings: Mapping from token strings to lists of
            ``(internal_id, term_frequency)`` pairs. Lists produced by
            :func:`build_index` follow ascending internal-ID order.
        doc_lengths: Token count for each internal document ID.
        internal_to_external: External ``doc_id`` for each internal ID.

    Internal IDs are zero-based positions shared by ``doc_lengths`` and
    ``internal_to_external``. External IDs are the caller's original strings.
    The dataclass does not validate manually supplied structures; builders
    return aligned lists and valid posting IDs.
    """

    postings: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int]]]
    doc_lengths: list[int]
    internal_to_external: list[str]

    @property
    def document_count(self) -> int:
        """Number of documents, including documents with no tokens."""
        return len(self.internal_to_external)

    @property
    def average_document_length(self) -> float:
        """Mean token count, or ``0.0`` for an empty collection."""
        if self.document_count == 0:
            return 0.0

        return sum(self.doc_lengths) / self.document_count

    def document_frequency(self, term: str) -> int:
        """Return the number of postings for the exact term; unknown terms yield 0."""
        return len(self.postings.get(term, []))

def build_index(documents: list[dict]) -> InvertedIndex:
    """Tokenize documents and produce an in-memory inverted index.

    Args:
        documents: Ordered iterable of mappings with a nonempty string
            ``doc_id`` and string ``title`` and ``text`` fields. Extra fields
            are ignored.

    Returns:
        An :class:`InvertedIndex` whose internal IDs follow input order,
        lengths count title and body tokens together, and postings contain
        ``(internal_id, term_frequency)`` pairs in that same order.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If an item is not a dictionary.
        ValueError: If required fields are invalid or an external ID repeats.

    Empty input produces an empty index. Input mappings are not modified.
    The title and body are separated by a newline before tokenization.
    """
    postings: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int]]] = defaultdict(list)
    doc_lengths: list[int] = []
    internal_to_external: list[str] = []
    seen_doc_ids: set[str] = set()

    for document in documents:
        if not isinstance(document, dict):
            raise TypeError("Each document must be a dictionary.")

        doc_id = document.get("doc_id")
        title = document.get("title")
        text = document.get("text")

        if not isinstance(doc_id, str) or not doc_id:
            raise ValueError("Document 'doc_id' must be a nonempty string.")

        if not isinstance(title, str):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Document {doc_id!r}: 'title' must be a string."
            )

        if not isinstance(text, str):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Document {doc_id!r}: 'text' must be a string."
            )

        if doc_id in seen_doc_ids:
            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate document ID: {doc_id!r}")

        internal_id = len(internal_to_external)
        seen_doc_ids.add(doc_id)

        # The separator prevents a word at the end of the title from
        # merging with a word at the beginning of the text.
        tokens = tokenize(title + "\n" + text)

        internal_to_external.append(doc_id)
        doc_lengths.append(len(tokens))

        term_frequencies = Counter(tokens)

        for term, frequency in term_frequencies.items():
            postings[term].append((internal_id, frequency))

    return InvertedIndex(
        postings=dict(postings),
        doc_lengths=doc_lengths,
        internal_to_external=internal_to_external,
    )

class BM25:
    """Score matching documents with the Okapi BM25 formula.

    Args:
        index: In-memory index whose postings and document statistics are
            treated as read-only for this ranker's lifetime.
        k1: Positive finite term-frequency saturation parameter (default 1.2).
        b: Finite document-length normalization parameter in ``[0, 1]``
            (default 0.75).

    The implementation uses ``log(1 + (N - df + 0.5) / (df + 0.5))`` for
    IDF and sums the standard BM25 term contribution. Repeated normalized
    query terms count once. Results sort by descending score, with ties broken
    by ascending internal ID, preserving input order independently of external
    ID spelling. Zero-score documents are omitted.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        index: InvertedIndex,
        k1: float = 1.2,
        b: float = 0.75,
    ):
        """Create a ranker; invalid ``k1`` or ``b`` raises ``ValueError``."""
        if not math.isfinite(k1) or k1 <= 0:
            raise ValueError("k1 must be finite and greater than zero.")

        if not math.isfinite(b) or not 0 <= b <= 1:
            raise ValueError("b must be finite and between 0 and 1.")

        self.index = index
        self.k1 = k1
        self.b = b

        # Compute these once, rather than repeatedly during scoring.
        self.document_count = index.document_count
        self.average_document_length = index.average_document_length

    def search(
        self,
        query: str,
        top_k: int = 10,
    ) -> list[SearchResult]:
        """Return up to ``top_k`` positive-scoring matches for ``query``.

        Args:
            query: Text normalized with the index tokenizer.
            top_k: Maximum result count; nonpositive values return no results.

        Returns:
            Results containing internal ID, original external ``doc_id``, and
            BM25 score, in descending score order with deterministic ID ties.
            Empty/unknown queries and empty or all-zero-length collections
            return an empty list. Query terms are deduplicated after
            tokenization.

        Raises:
            TypeError: If ``query`` is not a string.
        """
        if top_k <= 0:
            return []

        # Sorting gives a deterministic accumulation order.
        query_terms = sorted(set(tokenize(query)))

        if not query_terms:
            return []

        if (
            self.document_count == 0
            or self.average_document_length == 0
        ):
            return []

        scores: dict[int, float] = defaultdict(float)

        for term in query_terms:
            postings = self.index.postings.get(term, [])

            if not postings:
                continue

            document_frequency = len(postings)

            idf = math.log1p(
                (
                    self.document_count
                    - document_frequency
                    + 0.5
                )
                / (document_frequency + 0.5)
            )

            for internal_id, term_frequency in postings:
                document_length = self.index.doc_lengths[internal_id]

                length_normalization = (
                    1
                    - self.b
                    + self.b
                    * document_length
                    / self.average_document_length
                )

                numerator = term_frequency * (self.k1 + 1)

                denominator = (
                    term_frequency
                    + self.k1 * length_normalization
                )

                scores[internal_id] += (
                    idf * numerator / denominator
                )

        # Smallest (-score, ID) means highest score, then lowest ID.
        best = heapq.nsmallest(
            top_k,
            scores.items(),
            key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0]),
        )

        return [
            SearchResult(
                internal_id=internal_id,
                doc_id=self.index.internal_to_external[internal_id],
                score=score,
            )
            for internal_id, score in best
        ]

def main():
    """Load SciFact splits, validate their references, and print an example.

    Returns:
        None: The function prints split statistics and one judged example.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If no qrels splits exist or the train split is missing.
        AssertionError: If a loaded split is empty or contains dangling references.
        ImportError: If the optional ``beir`` dependency is unavailable.
    """
    split = "train"

    qrels_dir = DATASET_DIR / "qrels"
    available = sorted(path.stem for path in qrels_dir.glob("*.tsv"))
    if not available:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"No qrels splits found in {qrels_dir}")
    print(f"Available relevance splits: {', '.join(available)}")

    if split not in available:
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"Split '{split}' is unavailable. Available splits: {available}"
        )

    corpus = queries = qrels = None
    for current_split in available:
        current_corpus, current_queries, current_qrels = GenericDataLoader(
            data_folder=str(DATASET_DIR)
        ).load(split=current_split)
        assert current_corpus, f"The corpus is empty for {current_split}."
        assert current_queries, f"No queries were loaded for {current_split}."
        assert current_qrels, f"No judgments were loaded for {current_split}."

        for query_id, judgments in current_qrels.items():
            assert query_id in current_queries, (
                f"{current_split} judgments reference missing query: {query_id}"
            )
            for doc_id in judgments:
                assert doc_id in current_corpus, (
                    f"{current_split} judgments reference missing document: {doc_id}"
                )

        print(
            f"{current_split}: {len(current_corpus):,} documents, "
            f"{len(current_queries):,} queries, "
            f"{len(current_qrels):,} queries with judgments"
        )
        if current_split == split:
            corpus, queries, qrels = current_corpus, current_queries, current_qrels

    print("\nDataset consistency checks passed for every available split.\n")

    print(f"Split: {split}")
    print(f"Documents: {len(corpus):,}")
    print(f"Queries loaded: {len(queries):,}")
    print(f"Queries with judgments: {len(qrels):,}")

    query_id = next(iter(qrels))

    print("\nEXAMPLE QUERY")
    print(f"ID: {query_id}")
    print(f"Text: {queries[query_id]}")

    print("\nRELEVANT DOCUMENTS")
    for doc_id, relevance in qrels[query_id].items():
        if relevance <= 0:
            continue

        document = corpus[doc_id]

        print(f"\nDocument ID: {doc_id}")
        print(f"Relevance: {relevance}")
        print(f"Title: {document.get('title', '')}")
        print(f"Text preview: {document.get('text', '')[:500]}")

def read_jsonl(path):
    """Read nonblank JSON Lines records with their source line numbers.

    Args:
        path (Path): UTF-8 JSONL file to read.

    Returns:
        Iterator[tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]]: Source line numbers and decoded objects.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If a nonblank line is invalid JSON or is not a JSON object.
    """
    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as file:
        for line_number, line in enumerate(file, start=1):
            if not line.strip():
                continue

            try:
                row = json.loads(line)
            except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Invalid JSON in {path}, line {line_number}"
                ) from exc

            if not isinstance(row, dict):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Expected a JSON object in {path}, "
                    f"line {line_number}"
                )

            yield line_number, row

def convert_documents():
    """Convert the raw SciFact corpus and create its external ID mapping.

    Returns:
        tuple[set[str], int]: Document IDs and the count of empty documents.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If a record is invalid or contains a duplicate document ID.
    """
    input_path = RAW_DIR / "corpus.jsonl"
    documents_path = OUTPUT_DIR / "documents.jsonl"
    mapping_path = OUTPUT_DIR / "doc_ids.jsonl"

    seen_ids = set()
    empty_documents = 0

    with (
        documents_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as documents_file,
        mapping_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as mapping_file,
    ):
        for line_number, row in read_jsonl(input_path):
            location = f"{input_path}:{line_number}"

            doc_id = require_id(row, "_id", location)
            title = require_text(row, "title", location, default="")
            text = require_text(row, "text", location)

            if doc_id in seen_ids:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{location}: duplicate document ID '{doc_id}'"
                )

            internal_id = len(seen_ids)
            seen_ids.add(doc_id)

            if not title.strip() and not text.strip():
                empty_documents += 1

            document = {
                "doc_id": doc_id,
                "title": title,
                "text": text,
                "metadata": prepare_metadata(row, location),
            }

            mapping = {
                "internal_id": internal_id,
                "doc_id": doc_id,
            }

            write_jsonl_row(documents_file, document)
            write_jsonl_row(mapping_file, mapping)

    return seen_ids, empty_documents

    with output_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as output_file:
        for line_number, row in read_jsonl(input_path):

def convert_qrels(document_ids, query_ids):
    """Convert qrels splits and validate referenced queries and documents.

    Args:
        document_ids (set[str]): Valid document IDs from the converted corpus.
        query_ids (set[str]): Valid query IDs from the converted queries.

    Returns:
        dict[str, dict[str, int]]: Per-split counts of judgments, queries, and positives.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If qrels are missing, malformed, duplicated, or reference unknown IDs.
    """
    input_dir = RAW_DIR / "qrels"
    output_dir = OUTPUT_DIR / "qrels"

    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    split_paths = sorted(input_dir.glob("*.tsv"))

    if not split_paths:
        raise ValueError(f"No qrels files found in {input_dir}")

    split_statistics = {}

    for input_path in split_paths:
        split_name = input_path.stem
        output_path = output_dir / input_path.name

        seen_pairs = set()
        split_query_ids = set()
        positive_count = 0

        with (
            input_path.open(
                "r", encoding="utf-8", newline=""
            ) as input_file,
            output_path.open(
                "w", encoding="utf-8", newline=""
            ) as output_file,
        ):
            reader = csv.DictReader(input_file, delimiter="\t")

            expected_fields = {"query-id", "corpus-id", "score"}
            actual_fields = set(reader.fieldnames or [])

            if not expected_fields.issubset(actual_fields):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{input_path}: unexpected columns "
                    f"{reader.fieldnames}"
                )

            writer = csv.DictWriter(
                output_file,
                fieldnames=["query_id", "doc_id", "relevance"],
                delimiter="\t",
                lineterminator="\n",
            )
            writer.writeheader()

            for row in reader:
                location = f"{input_path}:{reader.line_num}"

                query_id = row["query-id"]
                doc_id = row["corpus-id"]

                try:
                    relevance = int(row["score"])
                except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"{location}: invalid relevance score"
                    ) from exc

                if query_id not in query_ids:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"{location}: unknown query '{query_id}'"
                    )

                if doc_id not in document_ids:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"{location}: unknown document '{doc_id}'"
                    )

                pair = (query_id, doc_id)

                if pair in seen_pairs:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"{location}: duplicate judgment {pair}"
                    )

                seen_pairs.add(pair)
                split_query_ids.add(query_id)

                if relevance > 0:
                    positive_count += 1

                writer.writerow({
                    "query_id": query_id,
                    "doc_id": doc_id,
                    "relevance": relevance,
                })

        split_statistics[split_name] = {
            "judgments": len(seen_pairs),
            "queries": len(split_query_ids),
            "positive_judgments": positive_count,
        }

    return split_statistics

def main():
    """Convert raw SciFact files and write processed data with a manifest.

    Returns:
        None: Writes converted files and prints a conversion summary.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If a required raw input path does not exist.
        FileExistsError: If the output directory already exists.
        ValueError: If converted collections are empty or contain invalid records.

    Side effects:
        Creates a new ``data/processed/scifact`` tree containing converted
        documents, queries, ID mappings, qrels, and a manifest. It refuses to
        overwrite an existing output directory.
    """
    required_paths = [
        RAW_DIR / "corpus.jsonl",
        RAW_DIR / "queries.jsonl",
        RAW_DIR / "qrels",
    ]

    for path in required_paths:
        if not path.exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"Required input not found: {path}"
            )

    if OUTPUT_DIR.exists():
        raise FileExistsError(
            f"Output directory already exists: {OUTPUT_DIR}\n"
            "Inspect it before removing or renaming it."
        )

    OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True)

    document_ids, empty_documents = convert_documents()
    query_ids = convert_queries()

    if not document_ids:
        raise ValueError("The document collection is empty.")

    if not query_ids:
        raise ValueError("The query collection is empty.")

    split_statistics = convert_qrels(
        document_ids,
        query_ids,
    )

    manifest = {
        "dataset": "scifact",
        "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION,
        "created_at_utc": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "input_directory": str(RAW_DIR.relative_to(PROJECT_ROOT)),
        "documents": len(document_ids),
        "queries": len(query_ids),
        "empty_documents": empty_documents,
        "internal_id_assignment": "zero-based corpus file order",
        "splits": split_statistics,
    }

    manifest_path = OUTPUT_DIR / "manifest.json"

    with manifest_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as file:
        json.dump(
            manifest,
            file,
            indent=2,
            ensure_ascii=False,
        )
        file.write("\n")

    print("SciFact conversion completed.")
    print(f"Documents: {len(document_ids):,}")
    print(f"Queries: {len(query_ids):,}")
    print(f"Empty documents: {empty_documents:,}")

    for split_name, stats in split_statistics.items():
        print(
            f"{split_name}: "
            f"{stats['queries']:,} queries, "
            f"{stats['judgments']:,} judgments"
        )

    print(f"Output: {OUTPUT_DIR}")

def main():
    """Build an in-memory index and validate it against the processed manifest.

    Reads ``documents.jsonl``, ``doc_ids.jsonl``, and ``manifest.json``;
    prints index statistics and sample postings. Does not persist the index.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If any required processed file is missing.
        ValueError: If counts or internal/external ID mappings disagree.
    """
    documents_path = DATA_DIR / "documents.jsonl"
    mapping_path = DATA_DIR / "doc_ids.jsonl"
    manifest_path = DATA_DIR / "manifest.json"

    for path in (documents_path, mapping_path, manifest_path):
        if not path.is_file():
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"Missing {path}. Complete Step 4 first."
            )

    # build_index accepts an iterable, so it can consume the
    # documents produced by read_jsonl one at a time.
    index = build_index(read_jsonl(documents_path))

    with manifest_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as file:
        manifest = json.load(file)

    expected_count = manifest["documents"]

    if index.document_count != expected_count:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Document count mismatch: index has "
            f"{index.document_count}, manifest says {expected_count}"
        )

    # Step 4 assigned internal IDs in corpus-file order.
    # Confirm that build_index assigned exactly the same IDs.
    mapping_count = 0

    for mapping in read_jsonl(mapping_path):
        expected_internal_id = mapping_count
        actual_internal_id = mapping["internal_id"]

        if actual_internal_id != expected_internal_id:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Mapping entry {mapping_count} has internal ID "
                f"{actual_internal_id}, expected {expected_internal_id}"
            )

        if expected_internal_id >= index.document_count:
            raise ValueError(
                "ID mapping contains more documents than the index"
            )

        expected_doc_id = mapping["doc_id"]
        actual_doc_id = index.internal_to_external[
            expected_internal_id
        ]

        if actual_doc_id != expected_doc_id:
            raise ValueError(
                f"ID mismatch at position {expected_internal_id}: "
                f"index has {actual_doc_id!r}, "
                f"mapping has {expected_doc_id!r}"
            )

        mapping_count += 1

    if mapping_count != index.document_count:
        raise ValueError(
            f"ID mapping has {mapping_count} documents; "
            f"index has {index.document_count}"
        )

    print("SciFact index checks passed.")
    print(f"Documents: {index.document_count:,}")
    print(f"Distinct terms: {len(index.postings):,}")
    print(
        "Average document length: "
        f"{index.average_document_length:.2f} tokens"
    )

    print("\nExample terms:")
    for term in ("science", "evidence", "protein"):
        postings = index.postings.get(term, [])
        print(
            f"  {term!r}: {len(postings)} documents; "
            f"first five postings: {postings[:5]}"
        )

def main():
    """Parse a query, build the SciFact index, and print ranked results.

    The command accepts one query argument and an optional ``--top-k`` count.
    It rebuilds the full in-memory index for each invocation and uses result
    internal IDs to retrieve the corresponding source documents for display.

    Raises:
        SystemExit: For command-line parsing errors.
        FileNotFoundError: If the processed SciFact corpus is not present.

    Side effects:
        Writes progress and ranked result details to standard output.
    """
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Search SciFact using stratajanus BM25."
    )

    parser.add_argument(
        "query",
        help="Search query. Put multiword queries in quotes.",
    )

    parser.add_argument(
        "--top-k",
        type=int,
        default=10,
        help="Maximum number of results.",
    )

    args = parser.parse_args()

    if not DOCUMENTS_PATH.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"Missing processed corpus: {DOCUMENTS_PATH}"
        )

    # SciFact is small enough to retain the documents for display.
    documents = list(read_documents(DOCUMENTS_PATH))

    print(f"Building index for {len(documents):,} documents...")

    index = build_index(documents)
    ranker = BM25(index)

    results = ranker.search(
        args.query,
        top_k=args.top_k,
    )

    print(f"\nQuery: {args.query}")
    print(f"Results returned: {len(results)}\n")

    for rank, result in enumerate(results, start=1):
        document = documents[result.internal_id]

        print(
            f"{rank}. {result.doc_id} "
            f"| BM25 score: {result.score:.4f}"
        )
        print(f"   {document['title']}")
        print()

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
stratajanus currently implements the lexical retrieval path shown below. Dataset preparation is optional when supplying your own documents in the canonical format accepted by build_index.

flowchart LR
    A[BEIR SciFact source] --> B[prepare_scifact.py]
    B --> C[Processed documents JSONL]
    C --> D[build_index]
    D --> E[InvertedIndex]
    Q[Query string] --> T[tokenize]
    E --> R[BM25.search]
    T --> R
    R --> S[SearchResult list]
    S --> V[External ID and score]

docs.title: Dataset preparation
docs.text:
download_scifact.py downloads the BEIR source under data/raw/scifact/. prepare_scifact.py validates the corpus, queries, and qrels and writes processed JSONL/TSV files, a manifest, and doc_ids.jsonl. The manifest records that IDs are assigned in zero-based corpus file order. The prepared document schema has a string doc_id, title, and text, plus metadata.

Preparation is not part of build_index: callers may provide an ordered list of canonical document dictionaries directly. The index builder uses the title and body together, separated by a newline, and does not modify the input dictionaries.

docs.title: Tokenizer
docs.text:
The default tokenizer first applies Unicode NFC normalization, then Python lowercasing, then extracts non-overlapping matches of Unicode-aware \\w+. Letters, digits, and underscores can appear inside a token; punctuation and other non-word characters separate tokens. Repeated terms and occurrence order are retained. Index and query strings use this same function.

TokenizerConfig records the schema version and analysis settings. save_tokenizer_config writes the active settings as JSON, while verify_tokenizer_config raises ValueError if a saved configuration differs. The current scripts do not serialize an index or invoke configuration verification automatically.

docs.title: Inverted index and identifiers
docs.text:
InvertedIndex stores three aligned structures:

  • postings: a mapping from token to a list of (internal_id, term_frequency) pairs.
  • doc_lengths: token count for each internal ID, including zero for empty documents.
  • internal_to_external: the original external doc_id at each internal ID position.

Internal IDs are zero-based positions assigned in document input order. External IDs are caller-provided strings and are not used for posting order. Each term appears at most once per document's posting list, with its count as the second tuple element. Posting lists produced by build_index are in ascending internal-ID order. Empty documents retain their IDs and lengths but have no postings. Duplicate external IDs and malformed required fields raise errors.

document_frequency(term) is the number of documents containing the exact term, not the sum of its term frequencies. The average document length is the mean of all document lengths and is 0.0 for an empty index.

docs.title: BM25 retrieval
docs.text:
BM25 uses the Okapi BM25 sum with defaults k1=1.2 and b=0.75. For each distinct query token with postings, it computes

\[ \\operatorname{IDF}(t)=\\log\\left(1+\\frac{N-df(t)+0.5}{df(t)+0.5}\\right) \]

and multiplies that by the term-frequency saturation and document-length normalization contribution. Query tokens are generated by the same tokenizer, deduplicated, and sorted before accumulation. Unknown terms contribute nothing. An empty query, empty collection, all-zero-length collection, or nonpositive top_k returns no results.

Results omit documents with score zero and sort by descending score, then ascending internal ID. SearchResult.score is the computed ranking score, not a probability or calibrated relevance estimate. Its doc_id is the external ID and internal_id is the position used by the index and source document list. If the index's public mutable structures are changed after constructing the ranker, the cached collection statistics may no longer agree; treat the index as read-only during ranking.

docs.title: Scope and future work
docs.text: The implemented pipeline is lexical and in-memory. Persistent/compressed indexes, dense or hybrid retrieval, benchmark metric evaluation, reranking, RAG, and domain-specific financial analysis are not implemented in the current package. They can be explored as future extensions without implying that this codebase already provides them.

docs.title: Text analysis and indexing
docs.text: This page covers the tokenizer and inverted index used by BM25. For the ranking formula and complete data flow, see Architecture.

docs.title: Build an index
docs.text:
build_index consumes an ordered iterable of dictionaries. Each document requires a nonempty string doc_id and string title and text fields; additional fields are ignored. The title and body are joined with a newline, then analyzed as one document. This boundary prevents the final title word from merging with the first body word.

from stratajanus.index.inverted import build_index

documents = [
    {"doc_id": "paper-1", "title": "Search systems", "text": "An inverted index."},
    {"doc_id": "paper-2", "title": "Retrieval", "text": "Search finds documents."},
]

index = build_index(documents)
print(index.document_count)                 # 2
print(index.average_document_length)        # mean token count
print(index.document_frequency("search"))   # documents containing the term
print(index.postings["search"])             # [(0, 1), (1, 1)]
print(index.internal_to_external[0])        # "paper-1"

Internal IDs start at zero and follow input order. A posting is (internal_id, term_frequency); each posting list is in ascending internal-ID order. doc_lengths[id] counts all title and body tokens, and empty documents remain represented with length zero. document_frequency(term) counts the posting entries, not total occurrences. Empty input produces a valid empty index. Invalid item types raise TypeError; invalid required fields and duplicate IDs raise ValueError.

docs.title: Tokenization rules
docs.text:
tokenize applies Unicode NFC normalization, then Python's str.lower(), then finds non-overlapping matches of the Unicode-aware regular expression \\w+. Letters, digits, and underscores are included in tokens; punctuation and other non-word characters separate tokens. For example, COVID-19 becomes ["covid", "19"], 3.14 becomes ["3", "14"], and paper_123 remains one token. Repeated tokens are preserved in order. Non-string input raises TypeError; text with no word matches returns an empty list.

TokenizerConfig and CONFIG describe the active schema and settings. save_tokenizer_config(path) writes formatted UTF-8 JSON and creates parent directories. verify_tokenizer_config(path) raises ValueError if saved settings differ from the active configuration.

docs.title: BM25 and command-line search
docs.text:
The architecture page explains BM25's IDF, parameters, query term handling, result ordering, and score meaning. A processed SciFact collection can be searched with:

python scripts/search_scifact.py "evidence for a scientific claim" --top-k 10

That script loads the processed JSONL, builds the index in memory, and prints the result ID, BM25 score, and title. It requires the SciFact preparation workflow described in dataset documentation.

docs.title: API
docs.text: See the API reference for generated documentation of InvertedIndex, build_index, TokenizerConfig, tokenize, BM25, and SearchResult.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This guide uses the implemented package API with a tiny in-memory collection. For a full SciFact workflow, see the home page.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
stratajanus requires Python 3.13 or newer. From the repository root:

python3.13 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -e .
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

The package itself uses the standard library. The pinned requirements include the tools needed for tests, SciFact scripts, and documentation.

docs.title: Build an index and search
docs.text:
from stratajanus.index.inverted import build_index
from stratajanus.retrieval.bm25 import BM25

documents = [
    {
        "doc_id": "paper-1",
        "title": "Search systems",
        "text": "An inverted index supports retrieval.",
    },
    {
        "doc_id": "paper-2",
        "title": "Scientific evidence",
        "text": "Evidence supports a scientific claim.",
    },
]

index = build_index(documents)
ranker = BM25(index)

for result in ranker.search("inverted retrieval"):
    document = documents[result.internal_id]
    print(result.doc_id, result.score, document["title"])

build_index assigns internal IDs in input order and stores the original IDs separately. The result score is an uncalibrated BM25 ranking score. Repeated query terms count once; ties preserve input order. See the indexing guide for the tokenizer and posting format, and the API reference for all public package and script APIs.

docs.title: Search SciFact
docs.text:
After installing dependencies, fetch and prepare the dataset, then run the search script:

python scripts/download_scifact.py
python scripts/prepare_scifact.py
python scripts/search_scifact.py "evidence for a scientific claim" --top-k 10

The CLI builds the index in memory on each run. The data download and conversion steps write under ignored data/ directories. Dataset structure and preparation details are in SciFact data.

docs.title: Tests and documentation preview
docs.text:
python -m pytest
mkdocs serve

MkDocs Material and mkdocstrings are included in the pinned requirements.txt toolchain. To build a static documentation site, run mkdocs build --strict.

docs.title: Source
docs.text:
• Dataset: SciFact, distributed in BEIR's scifact format.
  • Download URL: https://public.ukp.informatik.tu-darmstadt.de/thakur/BEIR/datasets/scifact.zip
  • Retrieval method: beir.util.download_and_unzip, called by scripts/download_scifact.py.
  • Local extraction directory: data/raw/scifact/ (ignored by Git).
  • BEIR dataset documentation: https://github.com/beir-cellar/beir/wiki/Datasets-available
  • This repository keeps the downloaded source files unchanged. No acquisition date is asserted because it was not recorded when these files were downloaded.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
• corpus.jsonl: document IDs, titles, and text.
  • queries.jsonl: query IDs and text.
  • qrels/train.tsv and qrels/test.tsv: judged query-document relevance labels.

The dataset as extracted here has 5,183 documents, 809 training queries with judgments, and 300 test queries with judgments. scripts/load_scifact.py checks that every judged query and document ID resolves in the loaded source data and prints a training query with its positively judged documents.
